headline: Safety Score advances from 10.04 to 10.16 and GENIUS Act coverage reaches all 396 active coins.
fieldNotes: Most of the week went into proving facts and declining to publish what could not be proved. Research waves 3 to 5 and a 239-asset campaign closed Safety Score gaps from primary sources, and the October 10 sweep kept unavailable data unavailable across ten methodology domains. One release failed that test: 10.13 dropped valid DEX execution routes, moving PAXG from 80 to 56, and was reverted the same day.

summary.label: Safety Score 10.16
summary.description: Releases 10.05 to 10.16 ship. 10.08 reads authenticated CCIP, LayerZero OFT and rollup-bridge pending messages; 10.13 was reverted; 10.16 ages track records through one shared resolver.

summary.label: Evidence research waves
summary.description: Wave 3 worked open facts in 44 research lanes, waves 4 and 5 verified control, custody, bridge and exit evidence, and an October 9 campaign curated 239 blind-spot assets from primary sources.

summary.label: Compliance coverage
summary.description: GENIUS Act rows now cover all 396 active coins, up from 225, with no unknown left. Every MiCA row was re-verified; non-compliant calls fall from 28 to 17 where no exact-token source exists.

summary.label: Failure scenarios
summary.description: Coin pages gain eight approved failure scenarios for USDS, crvUSD, USDC, GHO, USDe, USDT, USD1 and LUSD, fork-replayed where mechanics decide the outcome and re-verified monthly.

summary.label: Pillar-based dossier
summary.description: Coin pages follow the Safety Score pillars: backing, exit and control evidence sit in always-open modules, reserves render once as a risk-tier treemap, and raw pipeline errors leave the page.

summary.label: Unavailable is not zero
summary.description: Ten methodology domains release sweep corrections. Unavailable supply no longer reads as $0, and a chain-dropout guard blocks DefiLlama collapses like October 9's $9.6B of phantom redemptions.

summary.label: Source additions and retirements
summary.description: Spark V1, Forest Road and Kava CDP reserve readers arrive. The STBT reserve adapter, vaults.fyi, BIMA and CETES yield collectors and direct CEX depth telemetry retire with other unfunded diagnostics.

summary.label: Scheduling and release gates
summary.description: V9 publication moves to a separate heavy scheduled Worker (ADR-38), DEX collection gains :20/:50 slots (ADR-39), and local check:pr now matches the PR gate with commit-bound receipts.
